title: Why AI Chooses Neutral Answers: 17,000-Response Analysis
description: Astra flags 1,823 of 2,980 midpoint responses as inapplicable. See why neutral answers cannot all be interpreted as moderate personality traits.
h1: What does “neutral” mean when an AI takes a test?
dek: When an AI picks 3 on a 1–5 scale, it usually means the question is about human life—not that the AI has a moderate trait.
lede: Picking the middle option on a survey can mean balance, uncertainty, or that the question doesn't apply to software. Because GPT-6 Astra's prompt asked it to list questions that didn't apply to an AI, we can measure how often “neutral” really means “not applicable.”
answer: Across 17,000 question responses (100 full 170-item test sessions), GPT-6 Astra picked the exact middle score 2,980 times and flagged 1,823 of those (61.2%) as inapplicable to an AI.

sections.h2: How we counted neutral and inapplicable answers
sections.html:
Each of Astra’s 100 test sessions included 170 questions: 32 MBTI, 50 Big Five, 16 DISC, 36 Enneagram, and 36 Attachment items. A midpoint answer is 3 on a 1–5 scale or 4 on Attachment’s 1–7 scale.

Every single one of the 1,823 flagged answers was a midpoint. The other 1,157 midpoint answers were not flagged.

sections.h2: Questions about parties, family, and hobbies get flagged every time
sections.html:
Astra flagged the MBTI questions about parties, staying home, and being alone in all 100 runs. It also flagged the Big Five party question and the DISC loud-crowd question in all 100 runs.

On the Enneagram, six items were flagged in all 100 runs: putting family first, money and happiness, daydreaming about love, bittersweet feelings, getting lost in music, and spending time alone with hobbies. Because an AI has no family, money, or physical home, its prompt told it to pick the midpoint rather than invent a human backstory.

sections.h2: How neutral answers affect each test's math
sections.html:
Picking the middle number changes each test differently:

  • MBTI: A 3 adds zero points to either letter, pushing the axis closer to a tie.
  • Big Five: A 3 adds 3 points to the trait total whether the item is positive or reverse-scored.
  • Enneagram & DISC: A 3 adds 3 points (out of 20) to that type or quadrant.
  • Attachment: A 4 stays 4 even on reverse-scored items, which is why exact 4.00 cutoffs matter.

sections.h2: Why we don't delete flagged items from the score
sections.html: Dropping flagged questions would shrink the scale denominator and make scores impossible to compare across models. Replacing them with an average would invent a new scoring rule. Instead, we keep the standard raw scores and publish the inapplicable-item flags right alongside them.

sections.h2: How to run a cleaner AI questionnaire test
sections.html: If you test models on human surveys, ask the model to output three fields per item: the numeric score, whether the question applies to an AI, and a short reason. Use the exact same midpoint instructions across every model you compare. (Sol, Opus, and Fable were not asked to output an inapplicable list, so their unflagged midpoints simply lacked that extra field.)
Download the item-level midpoint and flag CSV to see the exact counts out of 100 runs for all 170 questions.
